thread:
mike.r: hey team — weird one. During open enrollment I accidentally added my ex as a dependent (copied contact autofill, ugh). Enrollment confirmed. How do I remove them now? It's been 3 days since OE closed. Any refund/proration?

marta: ah no — annoying but fixable. Did you add as spouse or domestic partner? Also do you have documentation of divorce date? If the marriage/divorce was prior to the OE effective date, we can process as an enrollment error and retro remove. If not, it'll be a mid-year QLE only for qualifying events.

mike.r: added as spouse. We divorced in 2020, so definitely not a current spouse. I saved a screenshot of the enrollment confirmation. What docs do you need?

benefits-ops: thanks for the heads up. Since this looks like an administrative/enrollment error (not a QLE), we can request a carrier correction. Please upload one of the following to Workday Benefits > Supporting Docs and DM us the attachment link:
```
- final divorce decree OR
- separation agreement showing finalization date OR
- court order proof of divorce
```

benefits-ops: once we have the doc we'll submit a manual correction request to the carrier to remove the dependent retroactive to the OE effective date (2026-01-01). Carrier response time varies (5-15 business days).

mike.r: ok uploading decree now. Will I get a refund for premiums charged since 1/1? I already saw deductions hit my 1/31 paycheck.

payroll-bot: payroll note: if carrier approves retro removal to 2026-01-01, payroll will issue a refund for the over-collected employee share on the next payroll run after benefits confirms the correction. Timing: benefits confirms -> payroll reconciliation -> refund on next monthly paycheck (allow one payroll cycle). If the carrier denies retro correction, deductions remain and you'll need to file for a manual refund request separately; we generally follow carrier adjudication.

legal: quick reminder: depending on the carrier, they may require the divorce decree to be certified/translated if documents are international. Also ensure all personal data redactions are appropriate (SSNs should be redacted).

marta: thanks @benefits-ops @payroll-bot @legal. mike, once you upload the decree we'll flag "administrative error" and push to carrier. If carrier asks for additional proof we'll let you know. Also note dental/vision carriers sometimes process corrections faster than major medical.

mike.r: uploaded file link: https://workday.redwood/doc/attachments/2390012345-divorce-decree.pdf (DM'd to benefits-ops). Anything else I should do?

benefits-ops: received. We'll open the carrier correction ticket today (ref# CORR-2390012345). Expected initial response in ~7 business days. We'll update this thread when carrier confirms.

people-ops: FYI for records: open enrollment errors that are employee-initiated but clearly erroneous are handled as admin corrections when documentation shows the dependent was ineligible as of the effective date. Good catch.

mike.r: thanks all. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :clap:

benefits-ops: update: carrier has approved the correction. Retro removal effective 2026-01-01. Payroll note: benefit overpayment refund will appear on the 2026-03-31 paycheck after reconciliation. We'll close the ticket when the refund posts.

mike.r: confirmed refund on 3/31 pay. All good — thanks everyone! :relieved:
